questions.question: Which of the following statements are correct regarding festivals followed in Christianity? A. Easter is the day celebrated for the ‘Resurrection of Jesus Christ’. B. According to the Bible, ‘Three days after Jesus was crucified, he was resurrected’. C. Good Friday is to commemorate the day of crucifixion of Jesus Christ.
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding festivals followed in Christianity?

A. Easter is the day celebrated for the ‘Resurrection of Jesus Christ’.

B. According to the Bible, ‘Three days after Jesus was crucified, he was resurrected’.

C. Good Friday is to commemorate the day of crucifixion of Jesus Christ.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3 (A, B and C).

Key Points

  • Easter is celebrated for the resurrection of Jesus Christ, an event that is central to Christian belief.
  • According to the Bible, Jesus was resurrected three days after being crucified, an event that is commemorated as Easter.
  • Good Friday is observed to remember the day Jesus Christ was crucified, marking his sacrifice for humanity.
  • All the statements A, B, and C are correct regarding Christian festivals.

Additional Information

  • Easter
    • It is the most important festival in the Christian calendar, celebrating the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.
    • It is observed on the first Sunday after the first full moon following the vernal equinox.
    • The week preceding Easter is known as Holy Week, which includes Maundy Thursday (commemorating the Last Supper) and Good Friday (commemorating the crucifixion).
  • Good Friday
    • It is a Christian holiday commemorating the crucifixion of Jesus and his death at Calvary.
    • It is observed during Holy Week as part of the Paschal Triduum on the Friday preceding Easter Sunday.
    • It is also known as Holy Friday, Great Friday, Great and Holy Friday, and Black Friday.
  • Crucifixion of Jesus
    • Crucifixion is a method of capital punishment where the victim is tied or nailed to a large wooden cross and left to hang until death.
    • According to the New Testament, Jesus was crucified, died, and was buried, and on the third day, he rose again from the dead.
    • This event is central to Christian theology, symbolizing Jesus' sacrifice for humanity's sins and his victory over death.
  • Resurrection of Jesus
    • The resurrection of Jesus is the Christian belief that Jesus rose from the dead on the third day after his crucifixion.
    • This event is commemorated on Easter Sunday and is the cornerstone of Christian faith, signifying hope and eternal life.
    • It is described in the New Testament and is considered the foundation of Christian belief and theology.

questions.question: When is Kali Pooja celebrated in West Bengal region?
questions.questionHtml: When is Kali Pooja celebrated in West Bengal region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kartika Amavasya.

Key Points

  • Kartika Amavasya:
    • This significant day falls during the Hindu month of Kartik (typically October/November).
    • It is observed for ancestral rites, particularly to appease departed ancestors. Rituals like 'shraddha' (ancestral offerings), 'tarpan' (water libations), and 'pind daan' (food offerings) are performed to honor and seek blessings from ancestors.

Additional Information

  • Kartika Poornima:
    • This day marks the culmination of the Kartik month and is celebrated as Diwali, the Festival of Lights. Diwali symbolizes the victory of good over evil and the triumph of light over darkness.
    • Homes are illuminated with diyas (earthen lamps), and festivities include fireworks, prayers to Lakshmi (goddess of wealth), and the exchange of sweets.
  • Ashwin Amavasya:
    • ​ Also known as Mahalaya Amavasya or Pitru Amavasya, this day in the Ashwin month (September/October) is dedicated to ancestral rites.
    • It is believed that ancestors visit the Earth on this day, and rituals are performed to offer them respect and ensure their peaceful journey.
  • Ashwin Poornima:
    • This full moon day in Ashwin is known as Kojagiri Purnima in some regions.
    • It is a time for prayers to Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth. Women often observe fasts and perform special rituals to seek blessings for prosperity and well-being.

questions.questionHtml: When was the 120<sup>th</sup> birth anniversary of Shaheed Udham Singh celebrated in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 26 December 2019.

Important Points

  • On 26 December 2019, the 120th birth anniversary of Shaheed Udham Singh celebrated in India.
  • Shaheed Udham Singh was an Indian freedom fighter belonging to Ghadar Party. He was born in 1899 in the Sangrur district of Punjab.
  • Shaheed Udham Singh is known for his assassination of Michael O'Dwyer in London, on 13 March 1940. Michael O'Dwyer was responsible for the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in Amritsar in 1919. As revenge, he was killed by Udham Singh.
  • Michael O'Dwyer was an Irish Indian Civil Service officer and during 1913 and 1919 he was the former lieutenant governor of Punjab in British India.

​Additional Information 

  • On 26 November 2020, we celebrated Constitution day.
  • On 28 September 2020, we celebrated the 113th birth anniversary of birth Shaheed Bhagat Singh.

questions.question: World Philosophy Day is celebrated each year on the third _________ of November.
questions.questionHtml: World Philosophy Day is celebrated each year on the third _________ of November.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Thursday.Key Points

  • World Philosophy Day is observed on the third Thursday of November every year.
  • For 2021, it was observed on 18 November.
  • The day promotes an academic exchange of philosophy for the development of human thought.
  • World Philosophy Day was initially established by UNESCO on 21 November 2002.
  • Theme for World Philosophy Day 2024 - Wellbeing in Urban Living.
  • In 2005, the UNESCO General Conference declared the annual celebration of this event.

Additional Information 

  • ​World Philosophy Day will celebrate "different interactions of human beings in their social, cultural, geographical and political environment this year." 
  • ​Philosophy stems from Philosophia, a Greek word that actually means the ‘love of wisdom'.
  • The study of reality and existence, along with the nature of human thought, is necessary as it constitutes the essence of life.
  • The discipline of philosophy also fosters global interactions, dialogue and has the ability to bring significant changes in society.

questions.question: Eid ul-Fitr is celebrated on the first day of Shawwal, which falls in the ______ month of the Islamic calendar.
questions.questionHtml: Eid ul-Fitr is celebrated on the first day of Shawwal, which falls in the ______ month of the Islamic calendar.
questions.solution:
• Eid ul-Fitr is celebrated on the first day of Shawwal, which falls in the Tenth month of the Islamic calendar.
  • The Islamic, Muslim, or Hijri calendar is a lunar calendar consisting of 12 lunar months in a year of 354 or 355 days.
  • Eid ul-Fitr  is also called the "Festival of Breaking the Fast".
  • It is a religious holiday celebrated by Muslims worldwide that marks the end of Ramadan, the Islamic holy month of fasting (ṣawm).
  • The months of the Islamic calendar are  - 

  • Sl. NO

    Month

    Meaning
    1. 

    Muharram
    • Forbidden
    • A sacred month, so called because battle and all kinds of fighting are forbidden (ḥarām) during this month.
    2. 

    Safar
    • Supposedly named thus because pre-Islamic Arab houses were empty this time of year while their occupants gathered food.
    3. 

    Rabi-al-Awwal
    • The first spring
    • Also means to graze, because cattle were grazed during this month.
    • The month of Birth of Prophet Muhammad.
    4. 

    Rabi-al-Thani
    • The second spring
    5. 

    Jumada-al-Ula
    • The first of parched land
    • Jumādá may also be related to a verb meaning "to freeze" as water would freeze during this time of year.
    6. 

    Jumada-al-akhirah
    • The last of parched land
    7. 

    Rajab
    • Respect, Honour
    • Rajab may be related to a verb meaning "to remove", so called because pre-Islamic Arabs would remove the heads of their spears and refrain from fighting.
    8. 

    Sha’ban
    • Scattered
      Marked the time of year when Arab tribes dispersed to find water.
    9.

    Ramadan
    • Burning heat
    • Supposedly so called because of high temperatures caused by the excessive heat of the sun.
    • During this time, Muslims must fast from pre-dawn until sunset and should give charity to the poor and needy.
    10.

    Shawwal
    • Raised
    • Female camels would normally be in calf at this time of year and raise their tails
    11. 

    Zulqiddah
    • The one of truce/sitting
    • A holy month during which war is banned. 
    12. 

    Zulhijjah
    • The one of pilgrimage
    • During this month Muslim pilgrims from all around the world congregate at Mecca to visit the Kaaba.

questions.question: The Rajpath was decided to be a permanent venue for the Republic Day parade from which of the following year onwards?
questions.questionHtml: The Rajpath was decided to be a permanent venue for the Republic Day parade from which of the following year onwards?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is 1955.

Key Points

  •  The parade takes place every year on Republic day (26th of January) at Rajpath in New Delhi.
  • The parade is being organized by the Ministry of Defence.
  • The parade showcases a multi-hued image of the country's rich cultural heritage and military power.
  • This parade is presided over by the President of India.
  • The first Republic Day parade was held in 1950, but Rajpath was decided to be the venue in 1955.

Additional Information

  •  Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated 'Kartavya Path' on 8th September,2022.
  • It symbolises a shift from the erstwhile Rajpath being an icon of power, to the Kartavya Path being an example of public ownership and empowerment.​

questions.question: When was the National Hydrogen Mission (NHM) launched?
questions.questionHtml: When was the National Hydrogen Mission (NHM) launched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 15 August 2021.

Key Points

  • On August 15, 2021, Honorable Prime Minister launched, National Hydrogen Mission.
  • This is the first scientific assignment in India to address all characteristics of value chain of hydrogen-based mobility. 
  • With this mission, India is all set to goal the renewable energy sector and push to harness the power of hydrogen energy.  
  • This budget allotted 1500 INR crore for the development of renewable energy including hydrogen.
  • Hydrogen energy is predicted to reduce carbon emissions that are set to jump by 1.5 billion tons in 2021.

Additional Information

  • The National Hydrogen Mission will center on the generation of hydrogen from green power resources and link India's growing renewable capacity with the hydrogen economy.
  • Hydrogen is a clean alternative to methane, also called as natural gas.
  • It is the most abundant chemical element, approximate to contribute 75% of the mass of the universe.
  • Here on earth, large numbers of hydrogen atoms are contained in water, plants, animals and, of course, humans.​
